extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners (attorneys and agents) and USPTO disciplinary staff
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and obligations for practitioners practicing before the USPTO, including proper execution and submission of powers of attorney and terminal disclaimers, supervision of non-practitioner staff, and conduct that may lead to disciplinary sanctions. The document is a USPTO Final Order describing violations, legal conclusions, and agreed sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power of Attorney must appoint a registered practitioner
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'Declaration and Power of Attorney' must appoint a registered practitioner to represent the inventor; a power of attorney left blank does not comply with the Power of Attorney Rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office found the March 31, 2006 'Declaration and Power of Attorney' failed to appoint any registered practitioner because the power of attorney was left blank; Office communications (e.g., Notice to File Missing Parts and later communications) identify noncompliance with the Power of Attorney Rules (new rules effective June 25, 2004). Handwritten additions to an already-executed declaration are questionable and may be rejected as creating an unclear record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attorney of record requirement to sign a terminal disclaimer
rubrics_metrics.description: An attorney of record may sign a terminal disclaimer; a person who is not an attorney of record is not authorized to sign the terminal disclaimer on behalf of the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order notes that 'An attorney of record may sign a terminal disclaimer. 37 C.F.R. § 1.321(b)(1)(iv).' Respondent signed a terminal disclaimer when he was not the attorney of record, and the Office dismissed the petition to revive on that basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practitioner must supervise non-practitioner assistants appropriately
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner must give non-practitioner assistants appropriate instruction and supervision concerning the ethical aspects of their employment and is responsible for their work product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures employed in supervising non-practitioners should account for the fact that they do not have legal training. Failure to provide adequate supervision (e.g., allowing assistants to add the practitioner's name to a power-of-attorney space without proper reexecution) can be a basis for discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not handle legal matters without adequate preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner must not handle a legal matter without preparation adequate in the circumstances (37 CFR § 10.77(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The OED concluded Respondent violated 37 CFR § 10.77(b) by submitting filings (e.g., the terminal disclaimer and resubmitted declaration) without ensuring the filings complied with requirements. Adequate preparation includes verifying authority to sign and that required appointments are on file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid conduct prejudicial to the administration of justice
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners must not engage in conduct prejudicial to the administration of justice (37 CFR § 10.23(b)(5)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order finds that the respondent's actions—submitting a terminal disclaimer when not attorney of record and resubmitting a declaration with an added power-of-attorney entry—constituted conduct prejudicial to the administration of justice under the cited rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure accuracy and completeness of documents before filing
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners must review documents for execution dates, proper signatures, and completeness before submission to the Office (e.g., verify inventor execution dates and that appointment language is present).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent acknowledged failing to spot the inventor's execution date and submitted an already-executed 'Declaration and Power of Attorney' with his name later added in handwriting; the Office did not accept the later-submitted power of attorney because of record discrepancies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper procedure when petitioning to revive an application
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions to revive must be supported by the proper and complete documents (including any necessary power of attorney); lacking authorization will result in dismissal of the petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office dismissed the petition to revive the '664 application because Respondent was not authorized to sign the terminal disclaimer inasmuch as a power of attorney appointing Respondent had not been filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Settlement agreements must satisfy 37 C.F.R. § 11.26 requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A proposed settlement agreement that resolves disciplinary action must satisfy the requirements of 37 C.F.R. § 11.26 and set forth stipulated facts, legal conclusions, and sanctions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order states the proposed settlement agreement 'satisfies the requirements of 37 C.F.R. § 11.26' and resolves all disciplinary action arising from the stipulated facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disciplinary sanctions and public notice obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Sanctions for violations may include public reprimand and publication of the Final Order and Notices in the Official Gazette; the OED must give notice of public discipline to relevant disciplinary enforcement agencies, courts where the practitioner is admitted, and the public (37 C.F.R. § 11.59).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order specifies agreed sanctions: (a) public reprimand, (b) publication of the Final Order, (c) publication of a Notice in the Official Gazette, and (d) notice to disciplinary enforcement agencies and courts in the practitioner's admitting jurisdictions, citing 35 U.S.C. § 2(b)(2)(D) and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.20(a)(3), 11.26 and 11.59.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parties bear their own costs absent agreement otherwise
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise agreed, each party to the settlement shall bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of the agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order states 'The OED Director and Respondent shall each bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of this agreement.' This reflects how costs may be allocated in settlement dispositions.
